items.note: Ten-week quasi-experiment in which 118 Chinese EFL learners (ages 13-15) made picture books with GenAI under supportive versus reflective scaffolding (AI-configuration comparison, no no-AI arm); creative thinking and originality of artifacts assessed, analysis focuses on interaction with prior language proficiency.

Comparative user study in which 45 designers completed a conceptual design task with physical prototyping, standalone generative AI, and a hybrid physical-plus-AI method (likely within-person); the abstract does not say whether design outputs were scored for creativity, and N is below 50.

Chinese-language article comparing human-human dyads with human-AI collaboration on the alternative uses and product improvement tasks; human-AI collaboration produced higher mean idea novelty, with fluency and flexibility also scored (AI versus human partner); N, assignment, and whether the AI is generative are not stated in the abstract; PsyArXiv preprint 10.31234/osf.io/7x2v3 is the same work.

CHI 2022 system paper (StoryDrawer) with a 2x2 study of 64 children aged 6-10 varying two AI drawing strategies (AI-configuration comparison); reports more creative and elaborate ideas and outcomes, but whether the AI counts as generative and how outputs were scored needs the full text.

FIERO, a card game with a generative-AI interface, compared with online collaborative writing alone (N=60); higher idea fluency, novelty, and story plot coherence, but the AI effect is bundled with physical cards and game play; arXiv 2607.11837, ACM version DOI 10.1145/3831305.

Vague conference paper comparing AIGC-generated logo designs with manual designs on creativity and efficiency, plus user perceptions; it is unclear whether designers used AIGC (experiment) or AI output was compared with human output (context_ai_vs_human); probably weak, kept for full-text check.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, Springer page); search notes describe a pretest-posttest design with random assignment to AI NLP tool interventions on writing proficiency, including creative-writing facilitation; whether the tools are generative and whether creativity is scored separately is unknown.

Preregistered randomized experiment (n=400) comparing no AI with exposure to one or several AI interpretations while close-reading poems; the outcome is interpretive performance and pleasure, not creativity, so it may fall out as no_creativity_or_diversity_outcome at full text; CHI 2026 and arXiv 2603.06855 are the same work.

Mainly a model-side tool paper (LLM agent networks brainstorming AI risks, novelty versus single-LLM baselines), plus a small human study of 11 teams starting ideation from an LLM-framework risk list versus a practitioner-written list; treatment teams identified more and more systemic risks (count outcome); number of people and assignment not stated, far below 50 teams.

Preregistered lab experiment giving a random half of 124 university students ChatGPT access on novel creative tasks; access worsened performance for above-median creative-potential participants, and a post-interaction creativity-potential task was also measured (possible after_ai outcome); SSRN 4676053, check whether it is an earlier version of Zhu and Zou (2026, JEBO).
